recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless BR&R opens a new issue identifying concrete element-level datatype changes.
issue_request: FHIR-28582 asked BR&R to review whether elements in MedicinalProduct and MedicinalProductPharmaceutical, such as language, status, and property.type, should use code, Coding, or CodeableConcept. The final Published/Persuasive R5 resolution says the resources were reviewed on 11 Jan 2023 and their use of code, coding, and CodeableConcept was appropriate.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-28582 was found. The issue appears to have been applied as a work-group review rather than a datatype-changing commit. Current fhir.ini maps MedicinalProduct to MedicinalProductDefinition and MedicinalProductPharmaceutical to AdministrableProductDefinition, which are active current-build resources.
additional_context: Current source keeps lifecycle status as primitive code with required PublicationStatus bindings, while language, dose-form, and product characteristic/property concepts remain CodeableConcept with explicit value set bindings. The adjacent FHIR-28584 medication-definition CodeableReference issue is already represented on the combined branch and is not duplicated here. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-28582 discussion or conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the authoritative current StructureDefinition source already matches the Jira review outcome, and changing CodeableConcept elements to code would narrow modeled concepts without a later approved issue.

related_jiras.note: Nearby medication-definition datatype issue concerning CodeableReference; it mentions this broader review and is already represented on the combined branch, but it is a separate modeled-reference decision.
